Issued at 557 AM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

A cold front is crossing our forecast area this morning, draped from 
roughly southern Ontario into areas just southeast of Defiance, OH, 
Fort Wayne, and Marion, IN as of this writing. Behind the front we 
have light north-northwest flow, except near Lake MI where winds are 
picking up slightly near the lakeshore. Have some patchy fog around, 
mainly along/ahead of the front at this time. Visibilities at 
KGWB/KUSE/KOWX/KAOH are all less than 1 mile (several less than 1/2 
mile), and expect this to persist through around sunrise or until 
the front moves through. Issued an SPS for patchy dense fog until 
13z for areas roughly along/south of US 24 east of I 69. 

Otherwise, northwest winds strengthen through the afternoon as 
surface high pressure builds in rapidly behind the exiting cold 
front. Gusts up to around 20-25 mph are expected, especially near 
Lake MI and north of US 30. Accordingly, waves on Lake Michigan 
around 2 feet this morning should build to 3 to 5 feet by early 
afternoon, persisting into late this evening. Waves approach at a 45-
90 degree angle relative to shore, with wave periods around 6 
seconds. Expect a strong north to south flowing longshore current 
along the beach, and strong structural currents near piers and 
breakwalls (especially on the north side). Rip currents are 
expected. Those visiting the beach should plan to stay out of the 
water. Maintained the previously issued small craft advisory/beach 
hazards statement from late this morning into the late evening 
hours. 

Outside of a light shower along/near the front this morning, we'll 
remain dry until this afternoon/evening when a shortwave moves 
through aloft. Showers and maybe a couple thunderstorms develop near 
an fgen band along a frontal zone in in the 850-700mb range over 
IL/NW IN that drifts southeastward and weakens with time this 
afternoon/evening. Could see a rumble of thunder if we get steeper 
lapse rates around 6-7C/km in mid levels. Otherwise, much of the 
surface instability is to our southeast (near Lima, OH and along 
southern border), so don't expect any widespread t-storm development.

Depending on the speed of the wave, precipitation/storm chances end 
by 00-3z along our southernmost border in IN/NW OH. 

High pressure centers over the Great Lakes region then tonight into 
Monday night, shifting eastward gradually beneath an amplifying 
upper level ridge. The broad high initially is centered over the SE 
CONUS, and builds straight north into Ontario at 00z Tuesday, then 
begins to tilt on the north end towards the eastern seaboard through 
Wed/Thu, which will bring us into a more active pattern in terms of 
showers and storms. Models have an upper level low/surface low 
traversing the northern plains and Canadian Prairies, eventually 
reaching Hudson Bay by Tuesday night and onto Quebec by 
Wednesday afternoon. The upper level trough begins to breakdown 
the northwest periphery of the ridge as the low moves eastward, 
bringing a sfc cold front into our forecast area by Tuesday 
afternoon/evening. Decent warm air advection/moisture pumping 
into the area ahead of the front beneath the upper level ridge 
provides us with an unstable environment. The cold front has an 
ETA of 18-00z depending on the model, which would be favorable 
timing for maximizing available instability (Nam has 1500-2500 
J/kg ML CAPE around this time). Bulk shear is on the order of 
30-40 knots, with the best values further north in MI. SPC has 
our forecast in a marginal risk for severe weather accordingly. 
Mid level lapse rates aren't all that good (around 6.5C/km max),
and if the front arrives later it won't be as favorable 
instability wise. If we do have severe weather, the main threats
would be damaging winds. High temperatures Tuesday will be in 
the mid-upper 80s for most areas, with locations west of I 69 
south of US 30 potentially reaching the low 90s. Coolest in 
lower MI, where temps will be in the lower 80s. Heat indices 
along and west of I 69, south of US 30 could reach around 100 
degrees. 

The cold front will move into our area and stall out, models appear 
to initially stall it out generally along US 24 by Wednesday. As the 
upper level trough moves north, the ridge builds back in again and 
could force the boundary further north-orienting along the toll 
road. Either way, wherever it sets up we'll see favorable conditions 
for shower and thunderstorm activity. Flow becomes more zonal, which 
will help kick off any shower/t-storms through Thursday/Friday. Have 
the best chances (70-80%) late Tue afternoon (far west) into 
Wednesday morning-but expect values around 40-60% through Thursday. 
Thunderstorms are possible at times in this period. Highs will drop 
into the mid 70s and low-mid 80s Wed-Fri, then we'll be in the 70s 
by the weekend.
